location: facts.csv fact_ids {1010,1020,1030,1050,1060}-FY2023-EQ_ATTR and -EQ_ORD; dataset.json Banks.companies.*.ratios.ROE.FY2024 and sector.ratios_all.ROE.FY2024; workbook Banks_Sector D12, calc block EQ_ORD rows 213-222
finding: Methodology s.1 says each period uses the latest restated figure. The FY2025 annual statements restate equity at 1 Jan 2024 (= 31 Dec 2023) for five banks (IAS 8 corrections that revalued unlisted FVOCI equity stakes). facts.csv still holds the pre-restatement FY2023 equity for these banks. ANB's FY2023 equity was overridden to the restated figure, so the rule is applied unevenly. Because FY2024 equity is restated but FY2023 is not, the FY2024 average-equity denominator mixes two bases. FY2024 ROE is overstated by 0.06-0.14pp per bank (1010 15.98% vs 15.91%; 1020 7.94% vs 7.87%; 1030 11.78% vs 11.64%; 1050 11.28% vs 11.20%; 1060 13.01% vs 12.88%). Sector FY2024 ROE is 14.46% vs 14.42%. The total understatement of FY2023 equity is SAR 2,717.3m.
recommendation: Override FY2023 EQ_ATTR to the restated 1 Jan 2024 balances, as was done for ANB (override row 77). Flag them R with the IAS 8 reason, then rerun analyze.py and the workbook build. Then check every FY2024 R equity value for a matching opening restatement.

finding: Alinma's income statement prints the financing charge on its own line ('Impairment charge on financing, net of recoveries') and a separate line for other financial assets. IMPAIR_FIN uses the sum of both lines, so it equals IMPAIR_TOTAL in every period. That breaks the definition (ECL charge on financing). Differences: FY2025 +29.7m (+2.9%); 9M2026 +12.5m; 9M2025 +16.9m; FY2024 -0.55m; FY2022 -9.0m. Alinma COR FY2025 is 0.49% vs 0.48% on the correct basis. The sector effect is under 0.01pp.
recommendation: Remap 1150 IMPAIR_FIN to the 'impairment charge on financing' line for all periods, including FY2021 and FY2023, and keep IMPAIR_TOTAL as the sum.

location: facts.csv IMPAIR_FIN; config/metrics.csv IMPAIR_FIN; overrides rows 28-34 and 81-82
finding: IMPAIR_FIN is not on one basis across banks. BSF uses loans only, and Alinma should (see B-D-002). Riyad, Aljazira and Al Rajhi use 'financing and other financial assets'. SNB uses total ECL on investments and financing. ANB uses ECL including commitments and other financial assets (OREO is excluded by override). SAIB includes 'real estate and other losses' in FY2021-22, although the ANB override removes OREO for exactly that reason. Financing-only amounts from the notes for FY2025: 1010 1,364.702 vs 1,361.983 used; 1080 715.230 vs 692.660; 1180 1,061.535 vs 1,034.143. SAIB FY2022 credit losses were 165.796 vs 191.569 used. COR effects are at most 0.012pp per bank and under 0.01pp for the sector.
expected: One documented basis (preferably the ECL charge on loans/financing from the impairment note), or a stated per-bank basis
recommendation: Either source IMPAIR_FIN from the financing ECL note for every bank, or rename the metric 'credit impairment (face line)' and state the per-bank basis in Definitions. At least treat OREO the same way for SAIB and ANB.

location: facts.csv 1120-FY2024-DEPOSITS (R), 1120-9M2025-DEPOSITS (R), 1060-FY2023-DEPOSITS (R); dataset.json sector LDR and DEPOSITS growth; Banks_Sector narrative A86
finding: Funding reclassifications create breaks in the deposit series. Al Rajhi moved SAR 26,750m from 'due to banks' into customer deposits at 31 Dec 2024 (note 43). FY2023 and FY2022 were not re-presented. SAB FY2023 deposits are restated to 253,457m from 240,940m, but FY2022 is on the old basis. As a result, Al Rajhi FY2024 deposit growth is 14.3% (9.6% like-for-like) and SAB FY2023 growth is 18.3% (12.4%). Sector deposit growth is FY2023 8.4% (7.8%) and FY2024 8.9% (7.9%). Sector LDR is FY2023 98.7% (99.2%) and FY2024 103.6% (104.7%). The narrative 'loans moved from 96.7% ... to 106.5%' therefore mixes bases, and the like-for-like rise is larger. None of this is disclosed next to the LDR or deposit figures.
expected: Series break flagged; like-for-like deposit growth and LDR shown or footnoted
found: Restated values used without a break note; LDR trend presented as one series
recommendation: Add a series-break flag to LOANS/DEPOSITS/LDR for 1120 (FY2024) and 1060 (FY2023). Footnote the narrative LDR and deposit-growth statements with the like-for-like figures, or exclude the reclassified amounts from growth.
